But New York only has room under the second apron in team salary to keep one player. In order to keep both Brown and Wiseman, the Knicks would need to trade a player on a standard contract without taking back salary.  My read heading into the weekend: Wiseman is a lock to make the roster. There is strong support to add Brown as well. The Knicks would need to make a trade by Monday afternoon if they want to keep Brown. I think they will explore all avenues to make that happen.  It's logical to assume that the Knicks will move third-year wing **Pacome Dadiet.** But I believe New York will explore other deals — including trades involving third-year guard **Tyler Kolek** — this weekend and Monday.  The Knicks will be asking teams to take on a player without sending back salary. To get a deal done, New York may need to attach its own second-round picks (New York will have at least 11 second-round picks in the next seven drafts).  Something worth noting here: multiple teams (Charlotte Hornets, Los Angeles Lakers and others) are trying to attach second-round picks to work through a roster crunch. text: We all know how risky draft pick deals can be. You're trading a player for what is basically a lottery ticket (or more than one).  Some worked out real well for one team (besides the obvious PG deal working out for OKC, or KG/Pierce deal worked out for the Celtics), but what about those trades that are looked back on being a bad move for one team where the draft pick panning out would've changed the entire way people viewed the deal?  For instance, on the note of KG, the TWolves got 5 guys and 2 picks for him. Jefferson was the only guy to have a good career with the Wolves. But they also got the 6th and 28th picks in the draft. Let's say that 6th wound up being Steph or DeRozan. How much different would a KG deal have been viewed in that case? An obvious win win for both since the Celtics get the future HOFer who helped win a title, and the TWolves get Jefferson plus a future face of their franchise.  And not as drastic, but the Vince Carter deal for the Raptors, while they got the bottom of the barrel return for him player wise, what if those picks panned out? Instead of Joey Graham they get Danny Granger (07-12 Granger was an underrated played)?

text: I'm back, with the same question as last season: who does this sub hate most?  Westbrook opened at #1...again. Draymond was the sub's most hated player of the week 8 times. Nobody else got more than 3, but he still lost the season.  **Look up your guy or your team: [courtsentiment.com](https://courtsentiment.com)**  ---  ## Top 5 most hated (min. 5,000 comments)  | # | Player | Negative | Comments | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | James Harden | 55.3% | 40,814 | | 2 | Lu Dort | 53.2% | 19,745 | | 3 | Draymond Green | 52.6% | 27,187 | | 4 | Julius Randle | 52.3% | 10,577 | | 5 | De'Aaron Fox | 52.2% | 35,977 |  If you think most hated means most negative comments, then that would be Wemby with 49K. But that's what 166K comments will do, and his negative rate is only 29.9%.  Most loved: OGGGGG, 51.1% positive. He took it late. Dylan Harper led for seven weeks and finished at 49.1%; OG passed him in week 37, when the Finals doubled his comments in a week.  ---  ## What the data shows  **The Knicks series did it.** Watching that series I knew Harden's sentiment was going to be ugly. I just didn't expect it to win him the season. He was 17th on the board the week the playoffs started and 5th going into the ECF. He took #1 the week it tipped, at 70% negative, his worst week of the year, and never gave it back. Pistons fans on Harden for the season: 72.8% negative.  **Wemby is the sub's new main character.** LeBron was the most talked-about player last season. This season Luka led the running comment count for most of the regular season, LeBron took it over in the first round, and Wemby passed both of them the week the WCF started. He finished with 166K comments to LeBron's 112K, and the sub mostly likes him: 33.5% positive vs. 29.9% negative, and the most loved player of the week 10 times, more than anyone.  **No consensus villain.** Last year 22 of 30 fanbases hated Draymond the most. This year Harden leads 6, and 13 of the 67 players on the leaderboard top at least one fanbase.  ---  ## What's new  I took a lot of feedback from you guys last time and upgraded the dashboard to a real site.  - "Where's SGA/Luka?" Rank by rate, volume or polarization. - "It needs context." Every player page has his games: how the sub reacted to each one, next to his box score. - "Which fans hate him?" Every fanbase on every player, plus a grid of who hates who. - "Show me the comments." Real comments on every player, checked to actually be about him. Still some errors, but you can see them.  I also replayed the Finals Game 4 game thread comment by comment against the play-by-play (simcast style, no footage). [The room on De'Aaron Fox](https://courtsentiment.com/recaps/0042500404-de-aaron-fox/): 34% negative in the 2nd, 80% by the 4th.  ---  ## How it works  - 7.3M comments pulled → 2.1M mention one of 223 tracked players → 1.79M attributed to one player - Nicknames count: 721 aliases across the 223 players, so "haliban" and "halipotter" both land on Haliburton. - Classified with Claude Haiku 4.5 (Batch API); quoted comments verified with Claude Sonnet 5 - Cost: $295 - Full methodology: [How it works](https://courtsentiment.com/how-it-works/) · Code: [GitHub](https://github.com/oluobiri/nba-hate-tracker)  ---  ## Limitations  - 68.6% agreement with a blind hand-labeled sample of 509 comments (±5 points), 95.4% on which player the comment is about. Last season's 96% was on a test set that I used to tune the prompt. This is a random draw. The model undercounts positive comments by about 7 points and shows no measurable bias on negative ones. - Sentiment ≠ hate. Factual criticism ("he shot 2-15") counts as negative. - Equal weighting. A 500-upvote comment counts the same as a buried one. - Fanbase views only see flaired commenters, about 60% of the comments. - One subreddit and one season (2025-26). Last season isn't on the site yet. - Small samples swing. That's why I used floors: 5,000 comments for the leaderboard, 200 for a fanbase row, 30 for a weekly point.
